'''Loudon Love''' (born '''Loudon Love Vollbrecht''' on April 21, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Raptors 905]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wright State Raiders men's basketball|Wright State Raiders]].

==Early life==
Love's parents got divorced when he was in middle school and he moved from Vermont to Illinois with his mother, Laura Love.<ref name="ryan">{{cite news |last1=Ryan |first1=Shannon |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-wright-state-loudon-love-20180314-story.html |title=Wright State's Loudon Love brings his football background at Geneva to the basketball court |accessdate=February 19, 2020 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=March 14, 2018}}</ref> Love attended [[Geneva Community High School]], where he competed in basketball and football. As a junior, he averaged 11 points and 6.8 rebounds per game for a 30-win team. Love played [[offensive tackle]] on the gridiron and received a scholarship offer from [[Illinois Fighting Illini football|Illinois]]. In November 2015, Love was injured during the last play of Geneva's 41-22 Class 7A playoff loss to [[Bradley-Bourbonnais Community High School]]. An MRI revealed he tore his ACL, forcing him to miss his senior year in basketball.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Armstrong |first1=Rick |title=Geneva's Loudon Love-Vollbrecht suffers torn ACL |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/aurora-beacon-news/sports/ct-abn-boys-basketball-geneva-love-vollbrecht-st-1112-20151111-story.html |accessdate=February 19, 2020 |work=[[Aurora Beacon-News]] |date=November 11, 2015}}</ref> After receiving basketball offers from [[Northern Illinois Huskies men's basketball|Northern Illinois]], [[Western Illinois Leathernecks men's basketball|Western Illinois]], [[Northern Kentucky Norse men's basketball|Northern Kentucky]], [[UMBC Retrievers men's basketball|UMBC]], and [[UMass Lowell River Hawks men's basketball|UMass Lowell]], he committed to play under coach [[Scott Nagy]] at [[South Dakota State Jackrabbits men's basketball|South Dakota State]], and followed him to [[Wright State Raiders men's basketball|Wright State]] when he received the coaching job there. He legally changed his last name from Vollbrecht to Love, his mother's last name, in honor of her sacrifices growing up.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Archdeacon |first1=Tom |title=WSU's Love is death to backboards |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/tom-archdeacon-wsu-love-death-backboards/6EWelTaUtWmTITAuPazEsK/ |accessdate=February 19, 2020 |work=[[Dayton Daily News]] |date=November 9, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
Love was redshirted his first season at Wright State, spending the season trying to lose weight and get in shape by doing intensified workouts and going on a restricted diet. On January 7, 2018, Love scored 25 points and had 17 rebounds and five blocks in a win against [[Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball|Oakland]], earning [[Horizon League]] freshman of the week honors.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Archdeacon |first1=Tom |title=By any name, Wright State has a force in Love |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/archdeacon-any-name-wright-state-has-force-love/iIBprtXBt2juQuRHuS9o8N/ |accessdate=February 19, 2020 |work=[[Dayton Daily News]] |date=January 10, 2020}}</ref> As a freshman, he averaged 12.9 points and 9.8 rebounds per game on a team that finished 25-10 and reached the NCAA Tournament.<ref name="ryan" /> He was named Horizon League Freshman of the Year and Second Team All-Conference. As a sophomore, he averaged 15.1 points and 8.2 rebounds per game and had 12 double-doubles. Love was named to the First Team All-Horizon League and District 12 First Team by the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Love Honored by NABC |url=https://wsuraiders.com/news/2019/3/20/mens-basketball-love-honored-by-nabc.aspx |website=[[Wright State Raiders]] |accessdate=February 19, 2020 |date=March 20, 2019}}</ref>

On November 9, 2019, Love had 26 points and 14 rebounds in an 85–62 win over [[Miami RedHawks men's basketball|Miami (OH)]]. He fractured his elbow during a game against [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle]] on November 26 and missed several weeks.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Archdeacon |first1=Tom |title=Raiders' Love hopes to return from fractured elbow this month |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/archdeacon-raiders-love-hopes-return-from-fractured-elbow-this-month/X7Qa7lemj1ujBdxUwFBU3N/ |accessdate=February 19, 2020 |work=[[Dayton Daily News]] |date=December 14, 2019}}</ref> Love earned Horizon League player of the week honors on December 31 after a 22-point, 16-rebound performance against [[Green Bay Phoenix men's basketball|Green Bay]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hoeferlin |first1=Mackenzie |title=Raider Basketball: Loudon Love returns to success on the court |url=https://wsuguardian.com/raider-basketball-loudon-love-returns-to-success-on-the-court/ |accessdate=February 19, 2020 |work=Wright State Guardian |date=January 13, 2020}}</ref> Love had 21 points and nine rebounds during a win against [[Youngstown State Penguins men's basketball|Youngstown State]] on January 18, 2020, though coach Scott Nagy was upset with his performance.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Harris |first1=Doug |title=Wright State basketball: Nagy looking for more from Love |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/wright-state-basketball-nagy-looking-for-more-from-love/vOhtaCX71OfBpaDD9kRMUM/ |accessdate=February 19, 2020 |work=[[Dayton Daily News]] |date=January 22, 2020}}</ref> He was named Horizon League player of the week on February 17, after contributing 24 points and nine rebounds in a win over [[UIC Flames men's basketball|UIC]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Loudon Love named Horizon League Player of the Week |url=https://wsuraiders.com/news/2020/2/17/mens-basketball-loudon-love-named-horizon-league-player-of-the-week.aspx |website=[[Wright State Raiders]] |accessdate=February 19, 2020 |date=February 17, 2020}}</ref> Love was named Horizon League player of the year at the conclusion of the regular season.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Boyle [[File:Loudon Love.jpg|thumb|left|Love with [[Wright State Raiders men's basketball|Wright State]] in 2019]]
On January 9, 2021, Love collected his 1,000th career rebound in a win over [[Youngstown State Penguins men's basketball|Youngstown State]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Johnson Jr.|first=Andre|title= Loudon Love hits 1,000 rebound mark, Raiders win big |url= https://dayton247now.com/sports/content/loudon-love-hits-1000-rebound-mark-raiders-win-big |date=January 9, 2021|website=dayton247now.com|accessdate=January 10, 2021}}</ref> He scored a career-high 34 points and had 11 rebounds on January 30, in a 86–56 victory over [[Robert Morris Colonials men's basketball|Robert Morris Colonials]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Love scores 34 to lift Wright St. over Robert Morris 86-56 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401258556 |access-date=June 18, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 30, 2021}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 16.6 points, 10.1 rebounds, and 1.9 assists per game, shooting 56.5 percent. Love garnered Horizon League player of the year honors for the second consecutive season.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Harris |first1=Doug |title=Nagy: Love looking at pros, but hasn't made final decision |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/nagy-love-looking-at-pros-but-hasnt-made-final-decision/QYUFOR2Y5JCR5LWIM2RIU4TY64/ |access-date=June 18, 2021 |work=[[Dayton Daily News]] |date=May 9, 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Texas Legends (2021–2022)===
On July 16, 2021, Love signed his first professional contract with Stade Rochelais of the [[Nationale Masculine 1]] in France, but did not play for the team.<ref>{{cite web|first=David|last=Jablonski|title=Wright State's Love to start pro career in Europe|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/wright-states-love-to-start-pro-career-in-europe/LUS3K7JG7ZFD7LAUYSI7HLUHNM/|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=July 16, 2021|access-date=July 29, 2021}}</ref> He was selected 10th overall in the [[2021 NBA G League draft (October)|2021 NBA G League draft]] by the [[Texas Legends]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Loudon Love Selected 11th Overall in 2021 NBA G League Draft|url=https://wsuraiders.com/news/2021/10/23/mens-basketball-loudon-love-selected-11th-in-nba-g-league-draft.aspx|work=[[Wright State Raiders]]|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}}</ref> On January 31, 2022, Love was waived after suffering a season-ending knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|first=Brian|last=Sweet|title=Texas Legends skid as they host West Coast teams|url=https://thesmokingcuban.com/posts/texas-legends-skid-host-west-coast-teams|work=The Smoking Cuban|publisher=[[FanSided]]|date=February 7, 2022|access-date=February 13, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2021-2022 Texas Legends Transactions History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Texas-Legends/32/Transaction_History/2022|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 29, 2022}}</ref>
===Memphis Hustle (2023–2024)===
On October 30, 2023, Love joined the [[Memphis Hustle]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Hustle announce 2023-24 training camp roster|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-2023-24-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=November 7, 2023}}</ref>
===Carpegna Prosciutto Basket Pesaro (2024)===
On April 4, 2024, Love signed with [[U.S. Victoria Libertas Pallacanestro|Carpegna Prosciutto Basket Pesaro]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]].<ref>{{cite web|title=LA CARPEGNA PROSCIUTTO BASKET PESARO SI ACCORDA CON LOUDON LOVE|url=https://www.victorialibertas.it/la-carpegna-prosciutto-basket-pesaro-si-accorda-con-loudon-love/|website=VictoriaLibertas.it|date=April 4, 2024|access-date=April 4, 2024|language=Italian}}</ref>
===Niagara River Lions (2024)===
On May 13, 2024, Love signed with the [[Niagara River Lions]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=River Lions Announce Signing of American Forward, Loudon Love|url=https://www.cebl.ca/river-lions-announce-signing-of-american-forward-loudon-love|website=CEBL.ca|date=May 13, 2024|access-date=May 14, 2024}}</ref>

===Mexico City Capitanes (2024)===
On October 28, 2024, Love signed with the [[Mexico City Capitanes]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Capitanes CDMX|title=Presentando roster para nuestro Training Camp 2024 ⬇️ #EstoEsCapitanes|number=1850907877126598762|user=CapitanesCDMX|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=October 29, 2024|language=Spanish}}</ref>

===Cleveland Charge (2025)===
On February 20, 2025, Love signed with the [[Cleveland Charge]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Cleveland Charge|title=Welcome to The Land @love_loudon! #ChargeUp|number=1892651367421923334|user=ChargeCLE|date=February 20, 2025|access-date=February 21, 2025|language=English}}</ref>

===Raptors 905 (2025)===
On March 7, 2025, Love's rights were traded to the [[Raptors 905]]<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Raptors 905|title=https://x.com/Raptors905/status/1898129567199478191|number=1898129567199478191|user=Raptors905|date=March 7, 2025|access-date=March 9, 2025|language=English}}</ref>
